newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish data seen boosting foreign T-bill interest.
newsitem.headline: Polish data seen boosting foreign T-bill interest.

text.p: Foreign investors, expected to be encouraged by Poland's better than expected 1996 inflation and the fading possiblity of an interest rate rise, are likely to show marked interest in Monday's T-bill tender, analysts said.

They said domestic banks were not likely to be buying large amounts of treasuries at the 800 million zloty auction, exept for their corporate clients, because they preferred to place cash in much higher yielding central bank bills. @

"Domestic non-financials and foreign investor bids may dominate demand on Monday's auction, at which the treasury is likely to hold yields relatively flat," said Rafal Chodzidlo, senior dealer at Bank Slaski SA.

Analysts said large scale sales of treasuries to foreigners in secondary trade this week, estimated at $250-300 million, knocked down yields below primary auction levels for T-bills and would likely keep a lid on yields on Monday.

They said demand should roughly match the offer with foreign interest highest in the benchmark 52-week paper, last sold with an average yield of 19.91 percent, and corporates opting for the shorter bills.
At the last auction the average yield for the 13-week T-bill was 19.47 percent and 19.61 percent for 26-week paper.
"There may be demand for the benchmark from foreigners... but for now the best investment for them is bonds," said Wojciech Kowalczyk, senior treasury dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.

Analysts said foreign investors bought the majority of the 518 million zlotys of fixed bonds at Thursday's auction. Year-on-year inflation fell to 18.5 percent last year from 21.6 percent at the end of 1995.
This week's foreign capital inflow pushed the zloty to almost four percent from the parity rate, the highest level since its one-off appreciation in December 1995.
On Friday the zloty closed at high of 3.90/3.82 percent from the parity rate against Thursday's 3.63/3.53 percent.
It was at 2.9020/50 to the dollar, down from 2.9000/30 on Thursday and at 1.8110/20 to the mark, up from 1.8205/25. @

Analysts said the zloty would remain bullish next week if expected inflows from foreign investors materialise, but some said the rise may be limited by central bank intervention at four percent from the parity rate.
"Four percent is the market's psychological resistance, many players expect the central bank to intervene when the zloty strengthens to this level," one senior dealer here said.
